messages:
alex: Heads-up: we keep seeing a gap between logs and traces for requests routed through the edge. logs often miss trace_id so console links break. Any quick wins?

jin: Do we have patterns where headers get stripped? nginx/fastly sometimes drop `traceparent` or our `x-redwood-trace`.

marta: yep, the CDN strips unknown headers for some customers by default. also a few services use `X-Request-Id` instead of trace ids.

alex: I think we need an enrichment step at the ingest path that looks for trace headers + x-request-id and normalizes into a single field. then all logs and traces can reference that.

luke: Agree. We should standardize on `redwood.trace_id` in structured logs to avoid colliding with vendor fields. Put it into OTLP Resource attributes or LogRecord attributes when present.

jin: small proto nit: OTLP has `trace_id` on spans but not on LogRecord. Some exporters (older) drop LogRecord attributes. We should confirm OTLP exporter versions.

observability-bot: ingest-pipeline: new daily error spike for log enrichment service (5xx) at 2025-10-12T09:14:31Z :warning:

marta: ugh. if enrichment fails we can't block logs though — fallback must be just pass-through with a flag. but every team will complain about missing links.

alex: proposal: implement a lightweight enrichment service that:
- consumes logs from the collector
- if trace headers exist, copies/normalizes them to `redwood.trace_id` (lowercase hex no 0x)
- else, if `x-request-id` present, write `redwood.request_id` and emit best-effort span-link event
- write attribute under `otel.resource` for traces, and LogRecord attribute for logs

jin: +1. also add a deterministic normalization function: strip dashes, lowercase, pad to 32 hex chars. put in docs and artifact tests.

luke: for console UX, instead of expecting consumers to implement that field, we can add an index mapping: if log.redwood.trace_id exists show trace link; else if log.redwood.request_id -> search traces for span with attribute `request_id`. Might be heavier but avoids forcing changes in many services.

marta: cost note: searching traces by request_id is expensive at query time. we should prefer writing a join key during ingest. retention differences also matter — traces are 30d by default, logs 90d; linking older logs to traces won't work. we should surface this in the rollout announcement.

alex: good point. rollout plan:
1) infra-only prototype for enrichment (canary in us-west1)
2) update console to prefer `redwood.trace_id` then fallback to request_id lookup limited to last 7d
3) add docs + SDK snippets for languages (js, py, go) with snippet for structured logging

jin: example snippet to include in docs:
```
logger.info('handled', {"redwood.trace_id": trace_id, "route": '/v1/generate'})
```

marta: and another snippet showing OTLP exporter config for logs + resource attributes. mention versions >= 1.20.

luke: one more thing: sampling. if traces are heavily sampled, links will be false negatives. We should attach sampled flag in logs `redwood.trace_sampled=true/false` so console can indicate sampling state instead of hiding link.

alex: agreed. action items:
- jin: prototype enrichment service + normalization util (ETA 3d)
- marta: check exporters and CDN header policies, list customers impacted (ETA 2d)
- luke: console fallback design + cost estimate for request-id search (ETA 5d)

marta: tagging @security to confirm any PII implications of copying headers into LogRecord attrs.

alex: cool. I'll post a short playbook for the canary and add a dashboard tile: % logs enriched, % linked to traces, enrichment 5xx rate. :thumbsup:

luke: :thumbsup:

observability-bot: deploy-bot: enrichment-proto v0.1 deployed to us-west1-canary at 2025-10-12T10:02:03Z

alex: nice, keep thread updated with errors/metrics.

marta: noted. will open a follow-up thread for SDK snippets once we lock the field names.
